title: Fed against hunger, safe from fear
translation: For the custom of Quraysh, their custom of the winter and summer journey: let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear.
body: Tradition links **īlāf** to safe-conduct pacts Hāshim won for Quraysh’s caravans; **Patricia Crone** called that “wrong as exegesis”, though such pacts were likely real. Food and safety, then worship: Luther’s **First Article** says God provides and “defends me against all danger”, so “it is my duty to thank… serve and obey Him.”
question: Was īlāf a set of real caravan pacts, or a word later explained by stories? How does each reading change the call to worship?
source_label: Crone, BSOAS 70 (2007) · Small Catechism, First Article
reading: Uri Rubin, “The Īlāf of Quraysh: A Study of Sūra CVI”, Arabica 31 (1984)
